title: the restore by the runbook alone, timed, and compared

findings.claim: The restore page's commands are written trialbox restore and trialbox backup-verify, but no program trialbox is installed on the host; the working form is python3 -m tools.trialbox, which only other paragraphs of the same section use
findings.happened: bash: line 1: trialbox: command not found (exit 127), from /opt/trialbox as root, for both commands
findings.expected: a command the host runs as written, from the release folder as root
findings.expected_from: the RUNBOOK hub (commands run on the box from /opt/trialbox as root); §5's own Backup paragraph writes python -m tools.trialbox backup-keygen and python3 -m tools.trialbox backup-status

findings.claim: python3 -m tools.trialbox restore and backup-verify stop with ModuleNotFoundError: zstandard on a python3 that has only the host packages §1 names (PyYAML, cryptography); psycopg, which the restore's own row check uses, is not named either; no page says which Python runs the restore
findings.page_says: To see which pack: `trialbox backup-verify <file> --key <private key>` lists it
findings.happened: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'zstandard' (tools/trialbox/backup.py imports it at its top); shown on this machine's python3, which has PyYAML and cryptography and lacks zstandard and psycopg; not run on Ubuntu 24.04 itself
findings.expected: the host that §1 step 1 prepares can run the restore page's commands, or the page names where they run
findings.expected_from: RUNBOOK §1 step 1 (the host packages: python3-yaml, python3-cryptography); pyproject.toml (zstandard, psycopg)

findings.claim: Step 2's docker compose stop $(docker compose ps --services | grep -vx db), run from the release folder as the hub says, finds no compose project; the working form needs --project-directory deploy, as the rest of section 5 writes it
findings.step: step 2 (stop every service but the database)
findings.page_says: `docker compose stop $(docker compose ps --services | grep -vx db)`
findings.happened: no configuration file provided: not found (twice, exit 1); nothing was stopped
findings.expected: every service but db stopped, as the next step requires
findings.expected_from: the hub (commands from /opt/trialbox); §5's other compose lines (docker compose --project-directory deploy ...); H22-compose-cwd-unstated, the same gap in §1

findings.claim: trialbox restore needs TB_DB_URL and TB_HAPI_DB_URL in its environment, naming databases the host can reach; the restore page names neither, deploy/.env's TB_DB_URL names the host db (resolvable only inside the compose network) and the box's compose file publishes no database port, so a box restored by the page alone stops at step 3
findings.happened: restore: TB_DB_URL is not set: nothing to back up from the database (exit 1). After the lift (both URLs on the test stack's published 127.0.0.1:5433, which the box's own compose file does not publish) the restore ran and ended complete
findings.expected: the restore page names what the restore needs to reach the box's databases, or the restore finds them itself as backup-nightly does (docker compose exec db)
findings.expected_from: the restore's own message; tools/trialbox/backup.py's opening (TB_DB_URL, TB_HAPI_DB_URL, TB_PG_RESTORE_CMD 'on a box: docker compose --project-directory deploy exec -T db pg_dump'); deploy/docker-compose.yml (db has no ports)

findings.claim: A console session opened before the wipe still works after the restore, for each of the four roles (GET /account 200 with the old cookie): the restore brings the sessions table back and ends none, and the page does not say to end them
findings.page_says: Each database is emptied, restored and its rows checked before any folder moves
findings.happened: four sessions opened before the backup answered 200 after the restore (the restore took about two minutes, inside the console's 10-minute idle limit); the new sign-ins with password and code also worked
findings.expected: a session from before the wipe does not work after it: a restored box starts with no open session
findings.expected_from: card H-33 (the integrator's words: 'sessions from before the wipe must not work'); D-279 (a password change ends every session of the account)

findings.claim: The variable the restore needs to give the stores back to their services (TB_DB_ROLES_CMD) is named only in the paragraph after the six steps; a reader who follows step 3 as written runs the restore without it, and in PRODUCTION it then ends NOT complete (exit 4) and must be run by hand
findings.step: step 3 (the restore) and the paragraph 'Database roles after a restore'
findings.happened: the follower read the whole page first and set it for step 3 (the restore said service_roles applied); a restore without it was not run here (a TEST box)
findings.expected: what step 3 needs is in step 3
findings.expected_from: the same paragraph ('Without it a PRODUCTION restore ends NOT complete (exit 4)')

findings.claim: Step 2 ends 'Start them again after the restore.' with no command, and does not say that the role script and migrate of the paragraph after the steps come first
findings.page_says: Start them again after the restore.
findings.happened: the follower ran the inverse of the page's stop (docker compose --project-directory deploy start) after migrate; every service became healthy
findings.expected: the command, in the order the page wants it
findings.expected_from: the page's own later paragraph ('after a restore run it once after the role script: python3 -m tools.trialbox migrate')

findings.claim: The restore page's numbered steps have two step 4s (a missing pack, and events after the backup), so its steps 5 and 6 are its sixth and seventh
findings.happened: the text holds '4. If a pack is not there' (line 198) and '4. **Events after the backup (D-455).**' (line 201)

findings.claim: Section 5's list of what a backup leaves out on purpose does not name the lake's older generations (db/gen/), its reader links (db/.open/) or its lock file, which the backup's manifest lists as left out and which are missing after a restore
findings.page_says: the lake's `tmp/` spill and half-built snapshots
findings.happened: 3 of the lake's 80 files were not back after the restore (one older generation, one reader link, the lock file); backup-verify listed the first two under excluded
findings.expected: the page's list of what is left out matches the manifest's
findings.expected_from: backup-verify's own 'excluded' (lake generations, lake reader links)

findings.claim: RUNBOOK section 22 names its drills test_runbook_22_restore_timed and test_runbook_22_replacing_hardware, and no such test exists in the repository; plan 8 section 8c says to stop writing 'Drill: test_...' before the test exists
findings.step: RUNBOOK section 22 (the page around the restore)
findings.page_says: **Drill (T-213b):** none. The timed restore is not rehearsed by a test: it needs a real compose box with the
findings.happened: git grep finds the names only in the runbook pages and the two tabletop records, never in tests/
findings.expected: a drill the page names exists, or the page says it does not yet
findings.expected_from: plan 8 section 8c ('Stop writing "Drill: test_…" on a runbook page before the test exists')
